title: QSGD: Communication-Efficient SGD via Gradient Quantization and Encoding
authors: Dan Alistarh, Demjan Grubic, Jerry Z. Li, Ryota Tomioka, Milan Vojnovic

findings.claim: An unbiased stochastic quantizer with entropy coding needs about 2.8 bits per coordinate per iteration, at the price of at most 2x more iterations.
findings.quote: we use $\approx 2.8n$ bits of communication per iteration as opposed to $32n$ bits, and guarantee at most $2\times$ more iterations, leading to bandwidth savings of $\approx 5.7\times$.

quantities.condition: derived: 32n / 2.8n bits per iteration, vs fp32, every step, before the up-to-2x iteration penalty
net bandwidth saving vs fp32 after up to 2x more iterations (as stated)
QSGD with Elias coding; no per-worker memory (memoryless, unbiased)

findings.bears_on: A provable ~3 bits/param/step budget for compressors that keep no worker-side state, the regime closest to a block that holds no residual buffer.

findings.claim: The authors show the bits-versus-variance trade-off of their quantizer is close to an information-theoretic limit.
findings.quote: We show that this trade-off is inherent, in the sense that improving it past some threshold would violate information-theoretic lower bounds.
findings.bears_on: Suggests memoryless unbiased compression has a floor of order bits per parameter per step, so the far larger LLM ratios come from worker-held state (error feedback) or local steps.

findings.claim: End-to-end gains of memoryless quantization were modest, about 1.8x faster ResNet-152 training on 16 GPUs.
findings.quote: on 16GPUs, we can train the ResNet-152 network to full accuracy on ImageNet 1.8$\times$ faster than the full-precision variant.

quantities.condition: ResNet-152 ImageNet, 16 GPUs, to full accuracy

findings.bears_on: Caps what stateless per-step compression offers in practice at roughly an order of magnitude.

findings.claim: With error feedback, any compression operator converges at the SGD rate under standard assumptions.

authors: Wei Wen, Cong Xu, Feng Yan, Chunpeng Wu, Yandan Wang, Yiran Chen, et al.

findings.claim: Ternary gradients cut worker-to-server traffic 16x with a 2-bit code and about 20x at the entropy limit.
findings.quote: Theoretically, ternary gradients can at least reduce the worker-to-server traffic by a factor of ${32}/{log_{2}(3)}=20.18\times$. Even using 2 bits to encode a ternary gradient, the reduction factor is still $16\times$.

quantities.condition: 2-bit code for ternary gradients vs fp32; every step; worker-to-server direction
entropy limit 32/log2(3) vs fp32

findings.bears_on: Stateless ~1.6-2 bits/param/step per worker; a lower anchor for grad.compression_ratio without error feedback.

findings.claim: TernGrad loses no accuracy on AlexNet and under 2% on GoogLeNet.
findings.quote: applying TernGrad on AlexNet doesn’t incur any accuracy loss and can even improve accuracy. The accuracy loss of GoogLeNet induced by TernGrad is less than $2\%$ on average.

quantities.condition: GoogLeNet ImageNet with ternary gradients

findings.bears_on: Shows ~16x stateless compression is near-lossless only on some CNNs; no LLM evidence.

title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them
authors: Kaiyue Wen, David Hall, Tengyu Ma, Percy Liang

findings.claim: Matrix-preconditioned optimizers' speedup over well-tuned AdamW falls from 1.4x at 0.1B to 1.1x at 1.2B.
findings.quote: However, the speedup of matrix-based optimizers is inversely proportional to model scale, decreasing from 1.4× over AdamW for 0.1B parameter models to merely 1.1× for 1.2B parameter models.

quantities.condition: Muon/Soap vs AdamW at 0.1B
Muon/Soap vs AdamW at 1.2B, 8x Chinchilla

findings.bears_on: Optimizer m_A shrinks with scale; at frontier C it is near 1.

findings.claim: Against a well-tuned AdamW baseline no optimizer exceeds 1.4x.
findings.quote: Against our well-tuned AdamW baseline, the speedup of alternative optimizers does not exceed 1.4×

quantities.condition: maximum speedup of 10 optimizers, 0.1-1.2B, 1-8x Chinchilla

findings.bears_on: Caps published optimizer m_A claims of 2x at about 1.4x.

findings.claim: Lion and Adam-mini, with reduced optimizer state, are within 5% of AdamW; Lion's gap widens with scale and Adam-mini's narrows.
findings.quote: The two memory-efficient AdamW variants (Lion, Adam-mini)—despite their reduced auxiliary state—closely track the performance of AdamW, with a slowdown of at most 5% and sometimes even perform better than AdamW. Interestingly, Lion and Adam-mini show different scaling trends regarding model size: the disadvantage of Lion relative to AdamW widens while the disadvantage of Adam-mini over AdamW narrows.

quantities.condition: lower bound of Lion/Adam-mini relative efficiency vs AdamW, derived: 5% slowdown

findings.bears_on: Cutting optimizer state (lower state_bits_per_param) costs at most about 5% in m_A at these scales.

findings.claim: A fitted law predicts Muon falls behind AdamW at 7B in the 1x Chinchilla regime.
findings.quote: This scaling law predicts that when the parameter scale reaches 7B, Muon will actually result in a higher loss compared to AdamW in 1× Chinchilla regime.
findings.bears_on: Muon's m_A may fall below 1 near frontier scale.

findings.claim: Sophia underperforms AdamW at small compute and slightly outperforms it at larger model or data size.
findings.quote: We found that Sophia tends to underperform AdamW in smaller compute regimes and eventually slightly outperforms AdamW when either the model size or the data size increases.
findings.bears_on: Sophia's m_A is near 1, growing slightly with scale.

findings.claim: Soap's measured speedup is 1.2-1.3x at 300M-520M versus the claimed 1.4x.
findings.quote: The actual speedup of Soap on 300M and 520M models are 1.2 to 1.3×, which is only slightly lower than the claimed 1.4× speedup.

quantities.condition: Soap vs AdamW at 300M-520M, midpoint of 1.2-1.3

findings.bears_on: Soap m_A about 1.2-1.3 at sub-billion scale.

findings.claim: Independent measurement puts Muon's token efficiency over AdamW at 1.1-1.2x.
findings.quote: It is later shown independently in the work of Essential AI AI et al. [2025] that Muon’s token efficiency compared to AdamW is only 1.1 to 1.2×.
findings.bears_on: Muon m_A about 1.1-1.2.

findings.claim: SWAN's and Dion's 2-3x claims come from below-Chinchilla budgets where matrix optimizers gain most.
findings.quote: SWAN Ma et al. [2025] and DION Ahn et al. [2025] report 2-3× speedup over AdamW. The comparison between these two optimizers and AdamW is carried out on a smaller than 1× Chinchilla regime, where the speed-up of matrix-based optimizer may be larger.
findings.bears_on: Discounts SWAN and Dion m_A claims.

findings.claim: Tuned scalar optimizers average under 1.2x over AdamW.
findings.quote: After proper tuning, all scalar-based optimizers achieve similar optimization speeds to AdamW, with an average speedup ratio of less than 1.2×.
findings.bears_on: Scalar optimizer variants give m_A near 1.

title: Adam-mini: Use Fewer Learning Rates To Gain More
authors: Yushun Zhang, Congliang Chen, Ziniu Li, Tian Ding, Chenwei Wu, Diederik P. Kingma et al.

findings.claim: Adam-mini matches AdamW with 50% less memory by sharing one second-moment value per parameter block.
findings.quote: We propose Adam-mini, an optimizer that achieves on par or better performance than AdamW with 50% less memory footprint.
findings.bears_on: Optimizer state falls from 2 words to about 1 per parameter at m_A about 1.

title: Deconstructing What Makes a Good Optimizer for Language Models
authors: Rosie Zhao, Depen Morwani, David Brandfonbrener, Nikhil Vyas, Sham Kakade

findings.claim: Apart from SGD, Adam, Adafactor, Lion and Sophia perform comparably in optimum and hyperparameter robustness.
findings.quote: Our findings indicate that, except for SGD, these algorithms all perform comparably both in their optimal performance and also in terms of how they fare across a wide range of hyperparameter choices.
findings.bears_on: Optimizer m_A clusters near 1; SGD is the outlier below.

title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
authors: Jiawei Zhao, Zhenyu Zhang, Beidi Chen, Zhangyang Wang, Anima Anandkumar, Yuandong Tian

findings.claim: Projecting gradients to a low-rank subspace cuts optimizer-state memory by up to 65.5% for 1B and 7B pretraining.
findings.quote: Our approach reduces memory usage by up to 65.5% in optimizer states while maintaining both efficiency and performance for pre-training on LLaMA 1B and 7B architectures with C4 dataset with up to 19.7B tokens

quantities.condition: LLaMA 1B and 7B, C4, up to 19.7B tokens

findings.bears_on: Optimizer state is compressible a few-fold, not by orders of magnitude.

findings.claim: At 7B, rank-1024 8-bit GaLore matched 8-bit Adam perplexity after 150K steps.
findings.quote: after 150K steps, 8-bit GaLore achieves a perplexity of 14.65, comparable to 8-bit Adam with a perplexity of 14.61.

quantities.condition: per-matrix projection rank at hidden size 4096 (7B); subspace refreshed every 200 steps
derived: projected gradient r x n vs m x n with r=1024, m=4096, if it were communicated

findings.bears_on: Lossless low-rank gradients at 7B need rank ~d/4, so low rank alone gives ~4x per step, far below local-update methods.

findings.claim: The authors argue gradients become low-rank during training for certain architectures even though weights are not.
findings.quote: Surprisingly, while the weight matrices are not necessarily low-rank, the gradient indeed becomes low-rank during the training for certain gradient forms and associated network architectures.
findings.bears_on: Supports a low update.rank per step, but the practical rank needed (d/4) is high.

title: APOLLO: SGD-like Memory, AdamW-level Performance
authors: Hanqing Zhu, Zhenyu Zhang, Wenyan Cong, Xi Liu, Sem Park, Vikas Chandra et al.

findings.claim: APOLLO-Mini (rank 1) beats AdamW in pre-training with SGD-level memory.
findings.quote: Even its rank-1 variant, APOLLO-Mini, achieves superior pre-training performance compared to AdamW with SGD-level memory costs.
findings.bears_on: Optimizer state near zero at m_A about 1 (up to 7B, short budgets).
